paper.title: Backtesting
paper.note: Draft chapter for 2nd ed. of 'Numerical Methods and Optimization in Finance' (Gilli, Maringer, Schumann, 2019).
paper.type: METHODOLOGY — how to backtest correctly, not a single tradable strategy
paper.abstract: A rigorous treatment of what backtesting is, why it is difficult and perilous (over-fitting, look-ahead, survivorship, small samples), and how to do it defensibly (walk-forward, sensitivity analysis, replication, meta-analysis). Uses MA-crossover, CAPE valuation timing, and industry momentum as worked examples on US equity data.

key_findings.finding: Optimized backtests overfit trivially — even on random data
key_findings.evidence: MA-crossover (m=10/30) on random walks beats buy-and-hold ~50/50 (no edge). But grid-search optimizing fast in 1..20 and slow in 21..60 makes it 'beat' the market in ~95% of random runs (median excess +19%). The improvement is pure data-snooping.
key_findings.application: Never trust an in-sample optimized result. A grid search WILL find a winner on noise.

key_findings.finding: In-sample results are worthless; all backtests need out-of-sample
key_findings.evidence: Financial models are 'sensitive' — tiny input changes cause large result changes (e.g. Oct 19 1987 -20.5%). Missing the 10 best S&P days = -50% wealth; avoiding 10 worst = +80%.
key_findings.application: Every strategy must be validated out-of-sample via WALK-FORWARD: split into N subperiods, tune only on in-sample part, concatenate out-of-sample parts.

key_findings.finding: Test sensitivity, not the single best variant
key_findings.evidence: Goal is a model that works 'OK-ish' across many parameter variants, not the best-fit optimum. Grossly overfit strategies break down fast on new data.
key_findings.application: Sweep parameters and require the strategy to be profitable across a broad neighbourhood, not just at one cherry-picked point.

key_findings.finding: Survivorship bias inflates results ~7-8% per year
key_findings.evidence: Gilli & Schumann (2017): using only current index components (dropping bankruptcies) gave ~7%/yr survivorship bias on German HDAX. Daniel et al. (2009) found up to 8% inflation for momentum/buy-the-dip.
key_findings.application: Backtest on the assets that were tradable AT THE TIME, not today's survivors. For crypto: don't only test coins still listed.

key_findings.evidence: Historical equity reward-to-risk ~0.3. A claimed equity Sharpe of 6 is not credible. Outlandish returns / no drawdowns / weird parameter values are red flags.
key_findings.application: If a crypto strategy backtest shows Sharpe > 3 or no drawdown, suspect a bug (look-ahead, fee omission) before believing it.

key_findings.finding: Check code by running on random data ('can it see the future?')
key_findings.evidence: A correct strategy on zero-mean random data should NOT systematically beat buy-and-hold. If it does, you have look-ahead or a bug.
key_findings.application: Look-ahead detector: run the signal engine on synthetic random walks; mean excess return should be ~0.

key_findings.finding: Momentum (buy top-k by trailing return) is the most-replicated anomaly
key_findings.evidence: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993); Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) show industry momentum. Worked example: hold the 10 highest-return sectors over the past year, equal weight, rebalance monthly.
key_findings.application: Cross-sectional momentum is a defensible baseline strategy to test on a crypto basket.

recommended_methodology.walk_forward: Split history into N windows; each has in-sample (tune) + out-of-sample (evaluate). Concatenate OOS segments. Report OOS-only performance.
recommended_methodology.sensitivity: Evaluate a grid of parameters. A robust strategy is profitable across most of the grid, not at one point.
recommended_methodology.random_data_control: Run the strategy on zero-mean random walks. Systematic outperformance => look-ahead bug.

worked_strategies.ma_crossover: Long when fast MA > slow MA, else cash. Params (fast, slow).
worked_strategies.cape_valuation_timing: Exit market when CAPE in top quantile q (avoid high valuation).
worked_strategies.industry_momentum: Hold top-k assets by trailing return, equal weight, rebalance monthly.

integration_notes.hermes_trading: Implemented as hermes_trading/schumann_backtest.py — walk-forward + sensitivity + random-data look-ahead control, runnable on real Kraken data.
integration_notes.usage: Validates existing strategies (VWAP, momentum, MA-cross) with the paper's discipline before any capital is committed.
